_howto: Production Pay how-to guides. mode click = the user clicks the real button. optional = skipped when that part isn't on screen. Never reuse a step id.

guides.title: Set up farms and units
guides.blurb: Add your farms and their units, with their size and GPS location.

steps.title: Production Settings
steps.text: Farms and units live in Settings: the gear at the bottom of the menu. Click it.

steps.title: 1. New farm
steps.text: Click + Farm.

steps.title: 2. Its name
steps.text: Type the farm's name, for example Highlands. Then click Next.

steps.title: 3. Its units
steps.text: On the empty line under the farm, type a block, orchard or field name, its hectares, and press Enter. The cursor stays there for the next one. You can also paste several rows from Excel.

steps.title: 4. Draw it on the map
steps.text: Draw on map opens the satellite photos. Search the place, click dot by dot around the edge, pick its colour, then Done.

steps.title: 5. Save
steps.text: The bar across the top shows what you changed. Save shows a summary first, then saves.

steps.title: Many at once
steps.text: Data Tools › Import from Excel takes three columns (Farm, Unit, Hectares): check the list, it goes into the sheet, then Save.

guides.title: Create a team and add its members
guides.blurb: Create a production team, choose how its manager is paid, and add its members.

steps.title: Teams
steps.text: Teams live here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Team name
steps.text: Click + New Team (opened for you here). For example Harvest Team A.

steps.title: 2. Vehicle (optional)
steps.text: Type the vehicle and press Enter, for example the tractor or trailer the team uses. Add more than one if needed.

steps.title: 3. The manager's share
steps.text:
For team work:
• Normal: the manager is paid for the team's full quantity; the workers share it.
• Equal share: the manager gets an equal share, like a worker.
• Average only: the manager gets the workers' average share.

steps.title: 4. Save
steps.text: Click Save (or skip it if you're only practising), then click Next.

steps.title: 5. Open the team
steps.text: Click the team's row to set it up.

steps.title: Settings tab
steps.text: Rename the team, change its vehicle or the manager pay. Save changes shows at the top as soon as you change something.

steps.title: Add people
steps.text: The Add people tab: search by name or PIN, or filter by department. Tick people and click Add Selected.

steps.title: The team's manager
steps.text: On the Members tab, click the star next to a person to make them the team manager (click it again to undo). The manager is paid at the manager rate.

steps.title: Team history
steps.text: Under ···: Team history shows everyone who joined or left the team (and who was made manager), and when.

steps.title: Deactivate
steps.text: Also under ···: deactivate a team you no longer use. Its history is kept, and you can reactivate it from Deactivated.

guides.title: Add an activity and its rate
guides.blurb: Add what people are paid for, and keep its rates over time in the Pricing Ledger.

steps.title: Activities & Pricing
steps.text: Activities live here. Click it.

steps.title: Add Activity
steps.text: Click Add Activity.

steps.title: Activity Name
steps.text: What the work is, for example Apple Picking.

steps.title: Unit of Measure
steps.text: What it's counted in, for example bins, crates or trees. Quantities in Daily Production use this unit.

steps.title: Worker Rate
steps.text: What a worker earns per unit.

steps.title: Manager Rate (optional)
steps.text: What a team's manager earns per unit, if different.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Saves the activity with these rates from today. Click Save at the top (or close the window if you're only practising), then Next.

steps.title: Pricing Ledger
steps.text: When a rate changes, don't edit the activity. Add the new rate in its Pricing Ledger, with the date it starts. Click it on an activity.

steps.title: New rates
steps.text: The new worker and manager rate.

steps.title: Effective Date
steps.text: The first day the new rate applies. Days before it keep the old rate, so past production is never re-priced.

steps.title: Log Price
steps.text: Adds the rate to the ledger. The list below shows every rate the activity has had.

guides.title: Create a task
guides.blurb: Give work to a team or phone user: activities and targets, where, how it's paid, evidence and dates.

steps.title: Tasks
steps.text: Tasks live here. Click it.

steps.title: Create Task
steps.text: Click Create Task.

steps.title: 1. Task & place
steps.text: The steps are on the left; the summary under them shows what will be created. First the name: something the team will recognise, for example Morning Apple Harvest - Block 5.

steps.title: Asset tags and vehicles
steps.text: Optional. Type a tag and press Enter for equipment used on this task, and pick any vehicles that work on it.

steps.title: Farm and units
steps.text: Choose the farm (type in the list to search), then the units. Leave the units empty to cover the whole farm.

steps.title: 2. Activities & targets
steps.text: Click Add activity for each kind of work in this task, and give each one a target. The target drives the task's progress bar.

steps.title: 3. People & pay
steps.text:
Per person: each worker is paid for what they captured.
As a team: the team's total is shared equally among the members who clocked in that day, and the manager is paid by the team's manager setting.

steps.title: Who does it
steps.text: Assign a team, a phone user who captures for it, or both. Type in a list to search it.

steps.title: 4. Dates
steps.text: The task shows on the phones and in Daily Production from the start date. The finish date is its due date; it is marked overdue after that. The quick buttons fill in the finish date.

steps.title: 5. Phone evidence
steps.text: Whether a photo and a signature are optional, mandatory or switched off, and whether they are collected once at the end of the task or with every capture.

steps.title: Create Task
steps.text: Saves the task as Pending. It stays grey until the name, farm, an activity and the dates are in (the summary says what is still needed). Click Create task, or close the pop-up if you're only practising.

steps.title: Then
steps.text: While it's Pending you can edit or delete it. Start makes it In Progress, and Complete closes it. Click a task any time to see what's been captured.

guides.title: Check and commit a day to payroll
guides.blurb: Load a team's day, check clockings and quantities, fix what's wrong, then commit it to payroll.

steps.title: Daily Production
steps.text: Each day is checked and committed here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. The day
steps.text: Choose the day to check.

steps.title: 2. The team
steps.text: Choose the team.

steps.title: 3. Load Grid
steps.text: Click Load Grid.

steps.title: 4. Clockings
steps.text: Each person's clock-in and clock-out from Time & Attendance and the hours at work. Under them: where those hours went (time on tasks, normal time, overtime). Someone with no clockings isn't paid a share of team work that day. Click the times to correct them.

steps.title: 5. Quantities
steps.text: One column per task activity: what each person captured on the phone. Type a quantity in, or over a wrong one. On team-paid tasks the share is worked out for you and can't be typed over.

steps.title: 6. Work that wasn't planned
steps.text: New task creates a task for this team and day, for work the team did that isn't on one of its tasks yet. It then shows as a column here.

steps.title: 7. Hours and pay
steps.text: The last columns total each person's day: normal time, approved and potential overtime, Sunday/public holiday, then piece wage, time wage and the total. Once someone has a quantity, their time on that task is paid by quantity instead of normal time. They update as you type.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Show only the people who did piecework, and sort PINs by their numbers only.

steps.title: 9. Save Draft
steps.text: Keeps your changes without making them final. You can come back and carry on.

steps.title: 10. Commit to Payroll
steps.text: Makes the day final: its records lock and count towards payroll. Only commit once everything is right.

steps.title: If something was wrong
steps.text:
In Data Tools: Unlock committed reopens committed records so they can be changed. Revert Edits removes manual changes and puts back what the phones captured.

If the day falls in a locked payroll period (Employee Master › Payroll Periods), it can't be saved, committed, unlocked or reverted until that period is unlocked. You'll see who and which dates are affected.

guides.title: Run a production report
guides.blurb: Choose the dates, who to include and the report type, then view or export it.

steps.title: Production Reports
steps.text: Reports live here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Dates
steps.text: Choose the start and end date.

steps.title: 2. Who
steps.text: Click Filters for a department, team or task, or particular employees from the Employees list. Leave them on All for everyone.

steps.title: 3. Report Type
steps.text:
• Daily Detailed: each person's production per day.
• Employee Daily Evidence: the photos captured with it.
• Employee Summary and Activity Summary: totals for the date range, per person or per activity.
• Job Costing (by employee), Job Costing Summary (a matrix of people and jobs) and Job Costing Wages (hours × hourly rate per day; the Global Hourly Rate applies here when it's switched on).
• Global Summary: everything combined.

steps.title: 4. Sort
steps.text: Sort by in Filters sets how the rows are ordered.

steps.title: 5. Generate Report
steps.text: Click Generate Report to see it.

steps.title: 6. Export
steps.text: Export saves the report you've just generated as an Excel spreadsheet.

guides.title: Check job costing
guides.blurb: Load a date range, find running and flagged jobs, and correct them.

steps.title: Job Costing Timesheet
steps.text: The Job Costing Timesheet lives here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Dates
steps.text: Choose the start and end date.

steps.title: 2. Load Data
steps.text: Click Load Data.

steps.title: 3. What needs checking
steps.text:
Still Running and Flagged are the ones to look at.

A job is flagged when it ran over 14 hours or has no activity chosen. A job still running has no clock-out yet.

steps.title: 4. Flagged Only
steps.text: Show only the flagged jobs.

steps.title: 5. Open a person
steps.text: Click a person to see their jobs.

steps.title: 6. Correct a job
steps.text: To fix a time, type it straight into the clock-in or clock-out box in the Time column and press Enter. Use Edit for another day, or to choose the right unit or activity. Changed times also move the matching attendance clockings. Jobs closed by the automatic clock-out show Auto clock-out; fix their time here.

steps.title: 7. Export
steps.text: Save the list to Excel if you need it elsewhere.
